title: China threatens ‘resolute’ retaliation over the US robot ban, and it holds the rare-earth card

content_html:
The US wanted to keep Chinese robots out. Beijing’s answer: do this, and we will hit back where it hurts.

China has threatened “resolute” retaliation after Washington moved to bar imports of Chinese-made humanoid robots. Its commerce ministry called the measure discriminatory and warned it “severely” damages trade relations, the New York Times and CNBC reported.

The ministry demanded that the US withdraw the decision, and threatened countermeasures if it does not. It accused Washington of “overstretching the concept of national security” and said the move disrupts global supply chains.

What the US actually banned

The trigger was an FCC order this week adding foreign-made “advanced robotic devices” to its restricted Covered List. It blocks new humanoids and robot dogs from the import approval they need to be sold in the US. Already-approved models can stay.

The rule is broader than it first looked. It sweeps up almost any new wireless, software-controlled robot over 4.4 pounds that can sense its surroundings, from robot lawnmowers to sidewalk delivery bots to Chinese robot vacuums. The FCC did not name China, but Chinese firms dominate the category.

Washington’s case rests on two fears. One is that connected robots could act as Trojan horses for data collection. The other is that robotics is strategically vital in an AI-driven economy. Chinese firm Unitree, one of the leaders, has already been flagged by the Pentagon over alleged military ties.

China’s leverage

The threat carries weight because China holds real cards. Analysts say the two obvious levers are rare earths, where China controls supply, and market access for US giants like Tesla and Nvidia. Both would sting.

The timing is also bad for Chinese robot makers. “This is bad news for Chinese humanoid producers planning their IPOs in the coming months,” said Counterpoint’s Marc Einstein. Unitree and Agibot have filed to go public, and Hong Kong-listed UBTech briefly fell more than 6 per cent.

The awkward truth

There is a catch that makes the ban tricky to enforce. It has become nearly impossible to build a competitive humanoid without Chinese-made parts, such as sensors and joints. China is also miles ahead on robots, running more factory robots than the rest of the world combined.

The clash lands at a delicate moment. Trump is due to host Xi Jinping in September, and tensions are already high. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has floated sanctions over AI model “theft”. Trump, for his part, hinted this week at a softer touch on AI controls to keep the US ahead.

Robots are now their own front in the tech war. The US has drawn a line around its market, and China is signalling that it can make that line expensive.

content_html_zh:
美国希望将中国机器人拒之门外。 北京的回答是：这样做，我们就会回击痛处。

在华盛顿禁止进口中国制造的人形机器人后，中国威胁要进行“坚决”报复。 据《纽约时报》和 CNBC 报道，中国商务部称该措施具有歧视性，并警告称其“严重”损害贸易关系。

外交部要求美方撤回这一决定，并威胁称，如果不撤回，将采取反制措施。 它指责华盛顿“过度延伸国家安全概念”，并表示此举扰乱了全球供应链。

美国实际上禁止了什么

触发因素是美国联邦通信委员会(FCC)本周发布的一项命令，将外国制造的“先进机器人设备”添加到其受限制的涵盖清单中。 它阻止了新的人形机器人和机器狗在美国销售所需的进口批准。 已经批准的模型可以保留。

该规则比乍一看更广泛。 它几乎可以扫除任何重量超过 4.4 磅、能够感知周围环境的新型无线、软件控制机器人，从机器人割草机到人行道送货机器人，再到中国机器人吸尘器。 FCC 没有点名中国，但中国公司在这一类别中占据主导地位。

华盛顿的案件基于两个担忧。 一是互联机器人可以充当数据收集的特洛伊木马。 另一个是机器人技术在人工智能驱动的经济中具有重要的战略意义。 其中领导者之一的中国公司 Unitree 已因涉嫌军事关系而受到五角大楼的举报。

中国的杠杆作用

这种威胁之所以具有影响力，是因为中国掌握着实实在在的牌。 分析师表示，两个明显的杠杆是稀土，中国控制着稀土的供应，以及特斯拉和英伟达等美国巨头的市场准入。 两者都会刺痛。

对于中国机器人制造商来说，时机也很糟糕。 Counterpoint 的马克·爱因斯坦 (Marc Einstein) 表示：“这对于计划在未来几个月进行 IPO 的中国人形机器人生产商来说是个坏消息。” Unitree和Agibot已申请上市，香港上市的UBTech股价短暂下跌超过6%。

尴尬的真相

有一个问题使得该禁令的执行变得棘手。 如果没有中国制造的部件（例如传感器和关节），构建具有竞争力的人形机器人几乎是不可能的。 中国在机器人方面也遥遥领先，运行的工厂机器人数量比世界其他国家的总和还多。

冲突发生在一个微妙的时刻。 特朗普将于九月接待习近平，紧张局势已经很严重。 财政部长斯科特·贝森特对人工智能模型“盗窃”提出了制裁。 特朗普本周暗示将对人工智能控制采取更温和的态度，以保持美国的领先地位。

机器人现在在科技战争中占据了自己的前线。 美国已经在其市场上划定了界限，而中国则暗示它可以让这条界限变得昂贵。
